headline: Amazon's planned data center could become the biggest climate polluter in the U.S.
summary: The data center in Pecos County, Texas, will include an on-site natural gas plant permitted to release 33 million tons of CO2 annually, surpassing any other U.S. power plant.
details: As part of a planned data center in Pecos County, Texas, Amazon is investing in an on-site power plant. This plant could become the largest source of climate pollution in the United States, according to The New York Times.
The NYT reports that the plant is permitted to release 33 million tons of carbon dioxide per year. This figure is more than any other power plant in the U.S. is currently allowed to emit.

An Amazon spokesperson confirmed the data center will be powered by new on-site generation. They stated this approach "won’t raise electricity costs for Texas families," addressing a common concern about data centers.
AI's growing demand has already impacted Amazon's carbon emissions, which were up 16% last year. This goes against the company's pledge to eliminate its carbon emissions by 2040.
The spokesperson acknowledged that "The world looks different now than when we co-founded the climate pledge." However, they maintained that Amazon's commitment to its climate goals "hasn’t changed."

headline_marked: [[X replaces revenue-sharing program]] with 'Original Content Rewards' on Sept 8
headline: X replaces revenue-sharing program with 'Original Content Rewards' on Sept 8
summary: The new program, launching September 8th, requires creators to have 500 verified followers and 500,000 Home Timeline impressions from verified users in 90 days, focusing on original content.
details: X is ending its current revenue-sharing program for content creators, which has seen several changes under Elon Musk. It will be replaced by a new "Original Content Rewards" program, set to launch on September 8th.
To be eligible, creators must have at least 500 verified followers and 500,000 Home Timeline impressions from verified users within the last 90 days. Additional requirements also apply.

Under the new system, creators will earn revenue based on "qualified impressions" on "original content." Qualified impressions are unique views from Premium subscribers on the Home Timeline feed where at least 50% of the post is visible.

"Original content" includes original reporting, analysis, user-taken videos and photos, and creator-made graphics or illustrations, including memes. Commentary or reactions also qualify if they add something meaningful.

X states the program aims to shift focus away from exploiting loopholes and clickbait. The goal is to reward creators who bring original ideas and unique perspectives, rather than those who game the system.
Participants in the previous revenue-sharing model will continue to earn revenue through September 7th, before the new program takes effect.
